questions.q: What actually triggers an unattended, scheduled run of a deployed SSIS package?
options: SQL Server Agent, running a job with a step of type SQL Server Integration Services Package
SSDT automatically re-runs any package you've built once a day
The SSISDB catalog runs packages on its own fixed internal schedule
Windows Task Scheduler is the only tool that can run SSIS packages
questions.explain: Deploying a project to the SSIS Catalog doesn't make it run on its own — SQL Server Agent, via a job step of type SQL Server Integration Services Package, is what triggers execution on a schedule.

questions.q: Which Package Source setting matches this course's Project Deployment Model approach?
options: SSIS Catalog
File System
SQL Server (MSDB)
SSIS Package Store
questions.explain: SSIS Catalog points the job step at a package deployed to SSISDB — the destination every package in this course's Project Deployment Model targets.

questions.q: How does a job step resolve a parameter's value from a specific SSISDB environment like PROD?
options: On the Configuration tab's Parameters sub-tab, select Environment and choose the environment whose variable should supply the value
By hardcoding the value directly into the job step's command line
Environments can only be selected when the package itself is opened in SSDT
SQL Server Agent automatically picks whichever environment was used most recently
questions.explain: This is exactly where Lesson 30's environment/parameter pattern connects to scheduling — the job step's Configuration tab lets a parameter resolve from a chosen environment's variable rather than a hardcoded literal.

questions.q: What is the single most common reason a package runs fine in SSDT but fails when SQL Server Agent runs it?
options: Permissions — the job step's Run as identity often lacks access SSDT had under your own credentials
SQL Server Agent cannot run any package built after SQL Server 2016
Packages must be rebuilt specifically for SQL Server Agent before they can run
SSDT and SQL Server Agent use incompatible package file formats
questions.explain: SSDT runs as you, with your Windows credentials and mapped drives; the job step runs as whatever Run as identity you configured, which frequently lacks the same file, network, or database access — a dedicated proxy account with the right permissions is the standard fix.

questions.q: What does the job step's logging level setting control?
options: How much execution detail the SSISDB catalog records for each run (None/Basic/Performance/Verbose)
How many times the job retries on failure
Which environment the job step uses
Whether the job step runs synchronously or in the background
questions.explain: The logging level (None, Basic, Performance, or Verbose) determines how much detail gets recorded for each execution — exactly the data Lesson 45's monitoring reports read back.
